correctness.rationale: An ideal I of free class-two L_d=V_d⊕Λ²V_d is equivalent to A=π(I)≤V, W=I∩Λ²V≥A∧V and a graph of a lift A→(Λ²V)/W. For a=dim A and m_a=binom(d−a,2), this gives T_{a,d}=[d:a]_q Σ_{c=0}^{m_a}[m_a:c]_q q^{ac}. The central count is Σ_c[N:c]_q; a=1 has M=binom(d−1,2), q^{d−1}/(1−q^{-1}) multiplier asymptotically. Gaussian coefficients are q^{c(n−c)}/P∞ (1+o(1)) at their peaks, yielding theta_(n+h parity) q^{(n+h)^2/4}/P∞. The exponent difference is exactly −d³/4+d²−d/2. Convex endpoint bounds on m_a+a and a(d−a) control every a≥2 by an exponent Δ_d~d³/4, so rank-one ideals dominate all noncentral ideals and the stated probability with four-class theta modulation follows. q fixed; finite diagnostics alone do not certify d→∞.
